title: Anthropic Lifts Potential Compute Spend to $750B in Updated IPO Draft

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The artificial intelligence startup is pursuing more hardware and cloud capacity than its partners can currently provide, which could add $150 billion to its financial obligations, per The Wall Street Journal. An updated draft S-1 filing shows that total spending on computing power in the coming years could reach $750 billion. This updated estimate exceeds the $600 billion figure previously disclosed, as the company continues to negotiate new deals for capacity. Anthropic is tentatively targeting a November IPO at a valuation of up to $2 trillion.

The firm generated $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, but posted a net loss of $80.7 billion, of which $72 billion was due to noncash accounting charges. Its existing obligations include about $450 billion in noncancelable cloud agreements—including contracts with Google for $111 billion, Amazon for $110 billion, and Microsoft for $31 billion—and a $160 billion deal with Broadcom. Risk factors in the filing highlight that two unnamed customers provide 20% of revenue and that liabilities from catastrophic AI incidents may be uninsurable.

selectedTweets.text:
ANTHROPIC'S DRAFT IPO FILING SHOWS REVENUE UP ~15X AND AN $80.7 BILLION LOSS

Here's what's inside, per the WSJ

Anthropic generated about $16.3 billion in revenue in the first half of 2026, up from $1.1 billion a year earlier, according to a draft prospectus viewed by the Journal.

It also reported a net loss of $80.7 billion. About $72 billion of that came from accounting charges tied to convertible notes and other instruments it used to raise money.

The other big numbers:
• Nearly $9 billion spent on computing in the first half, more than in all of 2025
• About one-fifth of revenue came from just two customers
• Roughly $450 billion in cloud commitments over the next 7 to 10 years, including $111 billion with Google $GOOGL, $110 billion with Amazon $AMZN and $31 billion with Microsoft $MSFT
• Total future infrastructure costs top $600 billion

About a third of the filing is risk factors, including the risk of AI models causing real-world harm and growing political resistance to data centers.

The IPO could value Anthropic at up to $2 trillion.

selectedTweets.text:
WSJ just reported Anthropic’s infrastructure commitments could reach $750B.

Revenue is currently growing much faster than compute costs though.

H1 2026 vs. H1 2025:

> Revenue: $16.3B vs. $1.1B
> Compute + infrastructure: nearly $9B vs. $2.3B

They went from spending over $2 on compute for every dollar of revenue to about 55 cents.

The $450B cloud portion runs over 7–10 years. Average that out and you get $45–64B a year. Keeping those payments at roughly 55% of revenue would take $82–116B in annual sales, assuming even payments and excluding the other infrastructure commitments.

Most of those cloud deals are noncancelable. Some are payable “regardless of actual usage.”

Dario put it pretty bluntly when discussing a hypothetical $1T annual compute commitment: “If I’m just off by a year … then you go bankrupt.”
